subject: Community stewardship grant request for Meridian (credits)
messages:
From: Aidan Cross <aidan@meridian.dev>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 10 Jan 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Community stewardship grant for Meridian - initial ask

Hi Lauren,

I manage developer experience for Meridian (open-source conversational routing library). We're preparing a community demo tour and CI workloads that will hit the Redwood API for embeddings and reranking. Our maintainer team is volunteer-run and we don't have a budget to cover tokens for the next quarter.

Would Redwood consider issuing community stewardship credits or a short trial extension so we can keep CI and the demo site live during the tour? Rough estimate: ~100k tokens over 3 months (mostly embeddings + some generation), possibly more if the demos take off.

Repo: https://github.com/meridian-dev/meridian
Funding: entirely volunteer / donations via Open Collective
Intended usage: CI test runs, public demo pages, and docs examples

Happy to share more details. If theres a form or quick checklist I can fill out, point me at it and I'll get everything over.

Thanks,
Aidan Cross
Lead Maintainer, Meridian
aidan@meridian.dev

Attachment: none

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: Aidan Cross <aidan@meridian.dev>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Jan 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Community stewardship grant for Meridian - initial ask

Hi Aidan —

Thanks for reaching out and for the clear context. We run a community stewardship process for OSS projects; a few quick questions so I can triage this to the grants queue:

- Confirm the repo license (MIT/Apache/etc) and that Meridian is public
- Do you represent a non-profit org or an independent maintainer group? (Open Collective is fine)
- Expected monthly token pattern (burst for demos vs steady CI) — the 100k estimate OK as a ballpark?
- Any compliance constraints (e.g., cannot send user PII to hosted APIs)?

If everything looks good we can provision a self-serve credit grant (one-time top-up) or a 90-day trial extension. Ill loop in our stewardship reviewer (Marissa) once you confirm.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Account Executive, Developer Growth
Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.ai

Attachment: community-grants-checklist (link in next email)

From: Aidan Cross <aidan@meridian.dev>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: Samira Noor <samira@meridian.dev>
Date: Fri, 10 Jan 2026 11:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Community stewardship grant for Meridian - initial ask

Hi Lauren — thanks for the quick reply. Answers below:

- License: MIT, public repo (link above)
- Org: independent volunteer maintainers; we accept donations via Open Collective (https://opencollective.com/meridian)
- Token pattern: Mostly steady CI (~30k/month) with two spikes of ~20k each when the demo tour runs (one in Feb, one in Apr). So the 100k over 3 months is accurate.
- Compliance: We dont process user PII in the demo — synthetic data + community examples.

If helpful: were targeting the first demo week in mid-February and would ideally have credits active by Feb 1. If a trial extension is simpler wed take that too.

Appreciate you and the team looking into this.

—Aidan

Priyom,

Forwarding a request from Meridian (Aidan). Theyre MIT-licensed, volunteer-run, modest usage (~100k tokens over 3 months) and need credits by Feb 1 for a demo tour. Can you review for a community stewardship top-up? If approved, recommend either:

- One-time $500 credits (self-serve top-up) OR
- 90-day trial extension that covers the 100k tokens (your call based on precedent)

Not urgent but timeboxed (activation by Feb 1). FYI: no PII. Id like Marissa to sign off on community eligibility.

Thanks —
Lauren

From: priyom_das@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Fwd: Community stewardship grant for Meridian - request (approved with conditions)

Lauren —

I reviewed Meridian. Based on MIT license, volunteer maintainer model, and modest usage, I approve a one-time stewardship grant of $600 in credits (USD-equivalent). Conditions:

1) Project must include a short attribution line in the demo site and README: "Powered by Redwood Inference — community stewardship grant"
2) Credits are non-transferable and expire 120 days from activation
3) We require a short follow-up email with usage metrics after 90 days (tokens consumed, basic outcomes)

Ill prepare the grant document and activation token once Lauren confirms the wording. CCing Marissa for the eligibility nod.

—Priyom
Billing & Community Programs
Redwood Inference
